Works entirely on your phone. No account, no ads, and no internet permission at all.

CloudSaver is 100% offline - it does not even hold the INTERNET permission. Your photos, videos, names and locations never leave the phone. No analytics, no ads, no accounts. The app writes only to its own folders. Automatic safety snapshots are hidden files, so nothing shows up in your gallery or Files app unless you tap Export yourself. Originals are never deleted automatically. State snapshots contain only file names, dates, sizes and hashes - never your photos or thumbnails. One honest note: no Android app can be made impossible to decompile; CloudSaver protects you with least privilege and tamper evidence instead. Terms: the app is provided as is, without any warranty; keep checking your cloud backup yourself.

Everything happens on the phone. Video bitrate comes from output pixels × fps (H.264: 0.10 bits per pixel per frame, HEVC: 0.065). 1080p30 H.264 ≈ 6 Mbps. Photos are resized to the preset megapixel limit at JPEG quality 80-85.
H.264 plays on every device. HEVC is about 35% smaller at the same quality, but older devices may not support it. H.264 is the default.
EXIF, GPS and dates are always copied. Rotation is baked in upright. If a compressed file would be bigger, the original is copied as-is - an item is never lost.
It makes compressed copies of your gallery in Pictures/CloudSaver. Your cloud app backs up only that folder. Originals stay exactly as they are.
Never automatically. Only via the manual Free-up tool - you select, and Android\'s own dialog confirms.
No. Every copy gets the original capture date (EXIF + file date), so the cloud timeline stays correct.
On the Storage saver preset videos keep ~90-95% visual quality and photo loss is invisible. Details on the Quality page.
Only that much data enters the cloud folder per day (default 250 MB). It doubles as the upload network limit.

If there was no upload proof, CloudSaver makes the copy again. The original is always safe.
Normal for sideloaded APKs. Choose "More details" → "Install anyway". The app is offline and holds no network permission.

CloudSaver keeps hidden safety snapshots (in Pictures/CloudSaver/.cloudsaver and Documents/.cloudsaver) alongside Android Auto Backup, so clearing data or reinstalling restores your state by itself. Each snapshot carries a checksum; an edited or damaged one is ignored rather than trusted. Items that come back without proof of upload become UNKNOWN - those can never delete originals. Very rarely a phone refuses every hidden location; then you will see one visible Documents/CloudSaver/backup.json, which is safe to leave alone.
Uploads stop, and CloudSaver also stops deleting copies (safety pause). Make room in the cloud or upgrade the plan.
The cloud app\'s own "Free up space" deletes only uploaded files. Copies that disappear after "Confirm uploads" are the exact proof. Usage access adds data-count verification.
Does the app use the internet?
No. The INTERNET permission is removed from the manifest itself. Uploading is always done by your cloud app.
How much battery does it use?

Smart mode (the default) works freely while charging. On battery it only starts above 30%, with the screen off, and stops after 30 minutes of work a day - photos are lighter, so they may also run with the screen on. Battery Saver, a warm phone or a low battery pause it right away, and Home always tells you what it is waiting for. Charging only mode uses no battery at all.
Yes. Everything the gallery shows (all volumes) is scanned, and you can keep the CloudSaver folder on the SD card.
Why is the output folder never empty?
The anchor rule: the newest file of each output folder is never deleted, so the cloud app never forgets the folder. No dummy files.
HEIC is compressed (to JPEG). RAW, GIF, SVG and similar are copied as-is - nothing is ever dropped.

CloudSaver is built for end-to-end encrypted clouds that have no compression of their own; clouds like Google Photos and OneDrive already compress for you. Best fit (E2EE): Ente (recommended), MEGA, Filen, Proton Drive. Also works: Nextcloud, Immich, OneDrive, or any app that can back up one chosen folder. Google Photos and Dropbox cannot work - they cannot back up just one custom folder.
